channel.title: Wisconsin Public Radio - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Wisconsin Public Radio (wpr.org)

item.title: Wisconsin Badgers win back-to-back national championships
item.description: On Sunday, the UW Badgers women's hockey team won 3-2 against number-one seeded Ohio State in the NCAA Frozen Four tournament.

item.title: 'Our attorneys are drowning': Public defender's office disappointed after court personnel bill dies
item.description: A Republican lawmaker and the state public defender's office are among those expressing dismay about the apparent death of a bill that would have added more court personnel.

item.title: Jason's classical picks: Trumpeters
item.description: "Drivetime Classics" host Jason Heilman writes about his favorite trumpeters, including classic and contemporary recordings.

item.title: State Democratic Party trounces GOP counterpart in February fundraising
item.description: New federal fundraising data shows Wisconsin's Democratic party brought in nine times as much as the state's Republican party last month.

item.title: ‘Where the horror grows’: New anthology of scary story writers and places across Wisconsin
item.description: We learn about a new collection of 15 short horror stories by Wisconsin writers set across the state — from the Mississippi River to Door County and exurbs surrounding Milwaukee.

item.title: AI is growing. Universities of Wisconsin wants to help you understand it.
item.description: AI technology is developing so fast, experts say advances are becoming hard to measure. Recognizing this, the Universities of Wisconsin has launched a free series of videos for people who need a starting point.

item.title: Roundy's Supermarkets sued by federal government for employment discrimination against nursing mother
item.description: Roundy’s Supermarkets is being sued by the federal government for allegedly firing a nursing mother who asked to keep drinking water at her work station so she could stay hydrated to maintain her breast milk supply.

item.title: Cleanup of spill ongoing at Jefferson County egg farm amid bird flu outbreak
item.description: Cleanup is ongoing after a Jefferson County egg farm spilled thousands of gallons of wastewater amid an outbreak of bird flu.

item.title: Meet the outdoor enthusiast traveling to some of Wisconsin’s most remote places
item.description: Jack Steward is the content creator behind “Tiny Cabin Life” — a YouTube channel with nearly 350,000 subscribers that chronicles his trips to remote areas of Minnesota, Wisconsin and the Upper Midwest.

item.title: Harley-Davidson announces 'reduction in force' for global workforce
item.description: Harley-Davidson is announcing a "reduction in force" for employees who work for the company across the globe.

item.title: Poll: Chris Taylor leads Maria Lazar in Wisconsin Supreme Court race
item.description: Liberals currently hold a 4-3 majority on the court. If Lazar wins, that margin will remain the same. If Taylor wins, it will grow to 5-2.

item.title: After board votes down re-fluoridation, what's next for DeForest water?
item.description: After a "rollercoaster" of twists and turns in local politics, supporters of restoring fluoride to DeForest's water are turning their focus to an April 7 election.

item.title: This conservation practice boosts wildlife species on farmland, new research finds
item.description: University of Illinois researchers analyzed traces of DNA in rivers and streams to learn how strips of trees near water — called riparian buffers — impact land species.

item.title: Wisconsin has a new food assistance law, with a MAHA-inspired provision
item.description: The bill that Gov. Tony Evers signed into law Monday to increase state funding for food assistance came after months of public debate over how to implement a key component of President Donald Trump’s signature One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

item.title: Racine County man convicted on election fraud charges after ordering absentee ballots for other voters
item.description: Harry Wait, the Racine-area man who requested absentee ballots on behalf of other people to prove it could be done, was convicted Tuesday night on election fraud and identity theft charges.
